posts.title: M3D 6T SRAM With BEOL Pass-Gates at 2nm (Georgia Tech, Synopsys)
posts.summary:
Researchers from Georgia Institute of Technology and Synopsys published a technical paper titled “A Process-Aware Hybrid Si/IGO Monolithic-3D 6T SRAM with BEOL Pass-Gates for the 2nm Node.” Abstract Excerpt: The paper proposes “a monolithic-3D (M3D) 6T SRAM at the 2nm node” that integrates BEOL IGO pass-gates with an all-silicon nanosheet latch, buried power rails, and... » read more
The post M3D 6T SRAM With BEOL Pass-Gates at 2nm (Georgia Tech, Synopsys) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: A new monolithic-3D (M3D) 6T SRAM design for the 2nm node integrates back-end-of-line (BEOL) Indium Gallium Oxide (IGO) pass-gates with silicon nanosheet latches.
The design incorporates advanced manufacturing features including buried power rails and Ruthenium (Ru) interconnects to optimize performance.
The cell achieves a 25% reduction in footprint compared to standard silicon baselines and demonstrates a 42.2% improvement in write delay at the subarray level.

posts.title: Hybrid HBM-HBF Architecture in LLM Inference (University of Oxford)
posts.summary:
Researchers at the University of Oxford published a technical paper titled “Hardware-Managed Heterogeneous High-Bandwidth Memory and Flash in LLM Inference Systems.” Abstract Excerpt: “ High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) offers a denser alternative, providing 16x more capacity per stack at comparable bandwidth. In this work, we show that while replacing HBM with HBF can address the capacity... » read more
The post Hybrid HBM-HBF Architecture in LLM Inference (University of Oxford) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers have proposed a Heterogeneous Memory Architecture (HMA) that combines High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) with High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) to address memory capacity constraints in LLM inference.
While HBF offers 16x the capacity of HBM per stack, its inherent long-tail latency can starve GPU schedulers if used naively.
The proposed architecture utilizes a prediction-based migration policy to keep high-latency HBF data off the GPU's critical path, maintaining performance while increasing memory density.

posts.title: Cycle-Level Simulator for Distributed GPUs For AI Workloads (Purdue)
posts.summary:
Researchers from Purdue University published a technical paper titled “Architecting the Next Generation of Asynchronous, Distributed GPUs for the AI Era.” Abstract Excerpt: The paper presents a “cycle-level simulation framework” for modern GPU generations including Ampere, Hopper, and Blackwell. It also reports validation against physical silicon, including a “99% Pearson correlation coefficient” on H100 GPU... » read more
The post Cycle-Level Simulator for Distributed GPUs For AI Workloads (Purdue) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Purdue University has introduced a cycle-level simulation framework designed to model modern GPU architectures, including NVIDIA's Ampere, Hopper, and Blackwell generations.
The simulator provides high-fidelity performance modeling for distributed AI workloads, enabling architects to evaluate system-level bottlenecks.
Validation against physical hardware shows a 99% Pearson correlation coefficient with H100 GPU results, confirming the tool's reliability for future architecture research.

posts.title: Intrinsic Polarization Superjunctions Boost GaN-On-Silicon Power Devices (EPFL)
posts.summary:
Researchers from École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL) published a technical paper titled “Intrinsic polarization superjunctions in III-nitride heterostructures for efficient power electronics.” Abstract Excerpt: “III-nitride semiconductors combine a wide bandgap with low sheet resistance and, thus, can be used for efficient power electronics. Their lateral architecture also enables monolithic integration on cost-effective silicon. However,... » read more
The post Intrinsic Polarization Superjunctions Boost GaN-On-Silicon Power Devices (EPFL) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: EPFL researchers have developed intrinsic polarization superjunctions in III-nitride heterostructures to improve the efficiency of power electronics.
The technology addresses critical limitations in GaN-on-Silicon devices, specifically mitigating electric-field crowding and surface/buffer trapping effects.
This advancement enables better breakdown voltage and dynamic performance, facilitating the monolithic integration of high-efficiency power devices on cost-effective silicon substrates.

posts.title: BYD Denza to launch N8L EV in September, expanding 6-seat SUV lineup
posts.summary:
The existing N8L is offered only as a plug-in hybrid with flash charging; the EV version is expected to use BYD's latest flash charging technology.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Denza is expanding its N8L large 6-seat SUV lineup by launching an all-electric version in September, moving beyond the current plug-in hybrid (PHEV) configuration.
The new EV model will feature a 208-liter powered frunk designed for family utility, including a drainable compartment for outdoor gear.
While specific battery and range details remain undisclosed, the vehicle is expected to integrate BYD's latest 800-volt flash charging technology and second-generation Blade Battery.

The introduction of an EV variant aims to capture a larger share of the competitive Chinese family SUV market, building on the existing N8L platform which currently starts at 319,800 yuan for the flash-charging PHEV version.
